ownedComment.body: 1.0 Note on Mission Definition:

There is most likely an activity that happens before this stage that focuses on "mission needs"; that is, from an enterprise perspective, what opportunities (products) are going to be pursued and what capabilities are needed (new plants or production lines)? Those decisions are considered inputs to the process/models captured here. Those needs and objectives are externally specified and captured in pkgs 1.1 and 1.2.
1.1 Note on Business Analysis:

Business analysis, is the identification, characterization, and assessment of an operational problem or opportunity within an enterprise.
Essentially for us, it’s the written case that there is a need for a new plant (or production line or job shop) (or revamping an old plant) to support an existing or new product line. Why: new plant is more efficient, provides needed additional capacity, cheaper to distribute product from new location, some needed new capability. New plant that replicates existing plant to provide additional capacity, but “re-design” is in fixes/upgrades to existing plant.

Requirements – Capture Features and Functions of a system or component. Constraints – Define the Non-Functional aspects of a system or component, such as restrictions on technology, resources or techniques to be used.

Suppliers are concerned with a fair system to be certified as a "trusted" supplier, based on agreed-upon KPIs such as on-time delivery and quality performance
Clear communication of expected ramp and cost reduction
Expectations and formats for data sharing
Maintenance cares about maximizing asset availability and uptime

What are the concerns of Quality Operations Management?
When inspection should be performed?
What is the inspection method? What resources are required?
What is the inspection criteria?
What to do with product/component after inspect?
How to report/document inspection outcome?
When and what needs to be moved?
Operators and Equipment are available in sufficient quantity to meet performance requirements (cycle-time, on-time delivery, etc.)
Skill, capability, and capacity of resources to handle the mix of move requests
Uptime and readiness
Material Handling cares about correctly moving items from one location to another. Correctly := on-time, location, documentation & tracking
don't lose stuff; make sure it travels/delivered with correct paperwork, e.g. labeling hazardous materials
Concerns related to connectivity and distributed data management, including (data) safety, security, resilience, reliability, privacy, etc.

where and what can be built? land-use and aesthetics
e.g. ISO 14001

George: Postwave - Is the actual behavior manual soldering?
Eugenio: No. It just happen to be the next transformational step (manual or automated) after automated soldering (reflow or wave).
George: So what is the actual behavior?
Eugenio: Postwave happens to be an extension of the automated part placement on a circuit card where parts that are too big for machine placement are then assembled onto the board. In some instances it's manual and does include soldering, but in other instances it's semi-automatic (this is where sometimes the axial insertion and DIP come into play). Factories view semi- automated steps as automated for routestep naming purposes.

FROM CSRM: The behaviors package provides artifacts for establishing a relationship between a requirement and a behavior that refines the requirement
The behavior can be: - Expressed by a text-based Use Case Description document - Captured in a Use Case Diagram - Refined by an Activity Diagram
Use Case Description documents can be a simple narative, or have a more detailed format; see, e.g. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Use_case#Fully_dressed
At each level (of the system decomposition) there are: - Behavior packages containing Use Case Description documents and their listing table - Use Case packages containing Use Case Diagrams and their listing table - Activity packages containing Activity Diagrams and their listing table
